title: From source records to episode-based comparisons
claim: Claims about collaboration are traced through identified task episodes, while logs and geometry supply different checks from questionnaires and researcher interpretations.
placement: Section 4.4, before detailed log-processing paragraphs or at the transition into Section 4.5.
layout: Top-to-bottom main flow with two parallel check columns and a compact context lane on the right.

nodes.label: Identify the task record
nodes.detail:
Dyad + research condition + software attempt
Practice, replay and restart kept distinct

nodes.label: Build a connected episode
nodes.detail:
Proposal / builder / modifier
Before → after → local outcome

nodes.label: Check action and task meaning
nodes.detail:
Video/source anchors and researcher account
Keep each source clock visible

nodes.label: Check actions and states
nodes.detail:
Accepted grab–release pairs
Latest known piece state · selected geometry

nodes.label: Compare connected cases
nodes.detail:
Within each dyad, then across dyads

nodes.label: Write findings and interpretation
nodes.detail:
Separate reported observation, checked state
and explanation; retain source codes

caption: Analysis workflow. Source identification precedes episode construction so that software rounds, research conditions and later replay recordings are not conflated. Video and researcher accounts describe the meaning and order of local actions; accepted event pairs and reconstructed states check selected movements and configurations. Questionnaire responses and interview comments provide context for the case comparison. The separation between source-specific clocks, on-site acceptance and later geometric verification is retained in the findings.
not_to_imply: Independent second coding or inter-rater agreement.
A complete frame-by-frame coding of every recorded video.
Grab counts directly measure ideas, cooperation or intention.
Questionnaire ratings prove an action sequence.
The 3/6 versus 0/6 descriptive comparison is a causal effect estimate.
